summary: Fire Force lets anyone read the fire history of any part of Africa at a glance. It harmonises NASA FIRMS detections from two satellite sensors, MODIS and VIIRS, into one consistent record, and turns it into an interactive web application. Users draw an area on the map or enter coordinates, choose a period, and instantly get a week-by-week calendar of active fires. Each week is compared with the same weeks of other years to flag unusual periods as "high" or "critical". The app stays honest with the data: days without observations are shown as missing, never as "no fire", and every threshold is explained on the charts. Fire Force makes complex satellite data understandable and actionable, helping land managers, researchers and communities spot abnormal fire seasons earlier.
details:
• WHAT IT DOES

Fire Force is a web application that turns NASA FIRMS satellite fire detections into a clear, week-by-week calendar of active fires for any area of Africa. Users draw a zone on the map or enter its coordinates, choose a period, and get the answer instantly.

  • HOW IT WORKS

Detections from two sensors, MODIS and VIIRS (NOAA-21), are aggregated on a regular grid and harmonised into one consistent record: one sensor fills in where the other is missing after calibration, and days without observations are shown as missing, never as "no fire". For the chosen zone, each week is compared with the same weeks of other years to flag unusual periods as "high" or "critical". The app also shows records, the typical fire season and whether the sensors agree. Every threshold is explained directly on the charts, and results can be exported.

  • IMPACT

Fire Force helps turn raw satellite data into decisions. From its analyses, users can:

- identify high-risk periods and anomalies to guide the monitoring and control of forest and bush fires;

- follow thermal activity around volcanic areas;

- locate zones where slash-and-burn agriculture is frequent;

- and support many other uses in environmental monitoring and research.

  • TOOLS

Python (pandas, pyproj, shapely), DuckDB, FastAPI, PostgreSQL/PostGIS on Neon, JavaScript, Leaflet and Apache ECharts, with the code shared on GitHub.

  • CHOICES AND LIMITS

Due to limited infrastructure, in particular the online storage of a free PostgreSQL database, we reduced our scope to the African continent, to two sensors (MODIS and VIIRS NOAA-21), and to the period 2020 to 2025. Detections are aggregated on a coarse grid, so Fire Force highlights where and when to look closer; it does not replace ground observation.

  • WHAT'S NEXT

Fire Force is designed to grow: with more storage we plan to cover larger parts of the Earth and add the other VIIRS sensors, for a richer and longer record.
